info.title: Tessera agent API
info.description: One agent namespace served by `tessera serve`. For channels (messages, outbox), people (replies), other systems (webhooks) and for coding agents that test and troubleshoot agents (inspection, triggers, dev clock, metrics). Every /v1 call needs `Authorization: Bearer <TESSERA_API_TOKEN>` except webhooks, which are signed. A typical troubleshooting loop: GET /v1/agent, POST /v1/messages, GET /v1/runs?conversation=..., GET /v1/runs/{id} (the timeline explains every decision and call).

get.description: Namespace, generation, routable Functions (with their routing text and `after`), all Functions, triggers, plugin actions with effect classes, subjects, funnels, experiments, routing threshold.

post.description: Routes it (or delivers it to the conversation's waiting run) and returns the run's status and messages. The caller is trusted: the holder of the token verified who the user is. Send the channel's messageId: a retried delivery with the same ID in the same conversation is not handled again (the answer is {"duplicate": true}).

messageId.description: the channel's ID of the message; retries with the same ID are ignored

get.summary: Messages not acknowledged yet, by run
get.description: Includes messages produced in the background (timers, schedules, webhooks). Deliver, then POST .../ack.

parameters.name: conversationPrefix
parameters.description: only conversations starting with it (a channel's own, e.g. wa:), so other channels' unread runs never fill the page

get.description: The run and its timeline: every journal record with what it was in the definitions (input source, step, action) and a one-line summary: the router's choice with probabilities, reads, Jev decisions with the question and options, questions and replies, intents before effects, results and failures, milestones, messages.

post.description: from: user (the user answered a question) or human (a person answered a task; value may be JSON such as true or {"happened": true}).

taskHash.description: The task's hash from GET /v1/tasks; required for approvals

by.description: Who answers, recorded for audit. When the task's queue has roles (RFC-0006), by must be the id of a Team member holding one of the roles of the queues the task reached; otherwise 403.

post.summary: Forward a waiting task to another queue
post.description: A member of a queue the task reached hands it to another HumanQueue (the receptionist to the manager). The task stays the same (its hash); the new queue's members may then answer it. 403 when by may not answer the task.

post.summary: Start a schedule trigger now, by hand

post.description: Wakes due runs, starts due schedules, checks stuck subjects; `tessera serve` also does this every second.

post.summary: Move the clock forward (only with tessera serve --dev)
post.description: Then runs the scheduler, so waits, schedules and deadlines can be tested without waiting.

The JSON body becomes event.payload. Sign it: X-Tessera-Timestamp: <unix seconds, within 5 minutes>, X-Tessera-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256, with the trigger's secret, of timestamp "." key "." body>, where key is the Idempotency-Key (empty without one). Idempotency-Key (up to 128 of [A-Za-z0-9-_.:]) makes a repeated delivery start nothing. An unknown trigger answers 401, like a bad signature. A trigger with event delivers the payload to the runs waiting for that event with the same key and answers the first of them (runId empty when nobody waited and the trigger starts no Function); a trigger's key expression, when set, identifies the run instead of the Idempotency-Key.

parameters.name: X-Tessera-Timestamp
parameters.description: unix seconds; within 5 minutes of the server's time

post.description: Re-reads the definitions from disk (an edited file is tested without a restart) and plays every scenario, or those whose suite/scenario contains `only`, with the server's models and a budget per scenario (default $0.05, at most $1). Each scenario runs on its own in-memory journal: real runs are never touched. Returns pass/fail, failures, transcripts, plugin calls and cost per scenario.

get.summary: The inbox: tasks waiting for people
get.description: Oldest first, optionally for one queue (?queue=). Each task has its queue, kind (approve, answer, input, takeover), text, options, since, the next SLA stage and a hash. Answer with POST /v1/runs/{id}/reply {"from":"human", "value":..., "taskHash":..., "by":...}: an answer without the current hash is refused (409), so nobody approves something that changed and a late or retried answer never answers the next task.

get.summary: A task's page (HTML), from a signed link
get.description: The link in a notification. Shows the task; opening it changes nothing. Works until it expires (7 days) or the task is answered or changes.

post.summary: Answer a task from its page (HTML form)
post.description: Form fields: by (who answers, recorded), decision (approve|deny) for approvals, answer otherwise. Bound to the task's hash in the link.

get.summary: Everything the agent does, live: every journal record of every run after a cursor, explained
get.description: Poll it with ?after=<next>: each item has the cursor, the run (id, function, conversation, status now) and the record explained as in GET /v1/runs/{id} (what the definition says, what happened). The order is the order records were written, across runs. For a coding agent: follow a conversation while you talk to the agent, or watch timers, triggers and people's answers as they happen.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: the cursor of the last record seen (next of the previous answer, or the SSE id); 0 or absent: from the beginning

200.description: {items: [{cursor, runId, function, conversation, status, entry}], next}

get.description: text/event-stream: an event "record" per item (id = the cursor, data = the item as JSON), a comment every 15 seconds while quiet. Resumes after ?after= or the Last-Event-ID header. With curl: curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' .../v1/activity/stream

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: the cursor of the last record seen (next of the previous answer, or the SSE id); 0 or absent: from the beginning
